questions.text: Describe the functions of the High Court.
questions.text_as_printed: Describe the functions of the High Court. (A)

answer.value:
Functions of the High Court
Has original jurisdiction over disputes related to marriage, wills, and contempt of court.
Accepts and resolves appeals against judgments of subordinate courts.
Supervises subordinate courts within its jurisdiction, directs case transfers, ensures compliance with rules, and collects records.
Protects fundamental rights and issues writs to provide justice.
It performs the function of delivering justice by receiving various writ petitions.

questions.text: Explain the appointment and tenure of High Court judges.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the appointment and tenure of High Court judges. (A)

answer.value:
Appointment and Tenure of High Court Judges:
The Chief Justice of a High Court is appointed by the President based on the recommendation of the Collegium consisting of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court and four senior-most judges, along with the advice of the Union Council of Ministers.
Other High Court judges are appointed by the President based on the recommendation of the Collegium consisting of the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court and two senior-most judges, along with the advice of the Union Council of Ministers.
The retirement age of the Chief Justice and judges of the High Court is 62 years.
They can be removed by the President on the grounds of proven misbehavior or incapacity, on the recommendation of both Houses of Parliament by a special majority.

questions.text: Write about the power of judicial review of the Supreme Court.
questions.text_as_printed: Write about the power of judicial review of the Supreme Court. (D)

answer.value:
The power of the Supreme Court to examine whether the laws made by the legislature and the orders and decisions of the executive are constitutional or not is called judicial review.
If they violate the Constitution, the Supreme Court declares them unconstitutional or invalid.
Thus, the Supreme Court has the power to prevent unconstitutional laws of the legislature and orders of the executive.

India has a single judicial system for the entire country.
It is independent of the legislature and the executive.
The High Courts and subordinate courts function under the control of the Supreme Court.
The Supreme Court is the highest court and its judgments are final.
The Constitution, laws, customs and precedents are the bases for judicial decisions.

questions.text: Explain the powers and functions of the Supreme Court.
questions.text_as_printed: Explain the powers and functions of the Supreme Court. (A)

answer.value:
Powers and Functions of the Supreme Court
Original Jurisdiction: Resolves disputes between the Center and states or between states and interprets the Constitution.
Appellate Jurisdiction: Accepts appeals against judgments of lower courts, conducts hearings, and delivers verdicts.
Advisory Jurisdiction: Provides advice to the President on matters of public, constitutional, or legislative importance.
Judicial Review: Has the authority to review the constitutionality of laws passed by the legislature and orders or decisions of the executive.
Protection of Fundamental Rights: Protects fundamental rights by issuing special writs under Article 32 of the Constitution.
